abstract: The effects of epidermal growth factor (EGF) on clones from a human embryonal carcinoma-derived cell line (Tera-2) have been studied. Cells were plated at clonal densities, whereafter the effects of serum and EGF on cell locomotion and cell proliferation were examined. The addition of 50 ngEGF ml-1 resulted in increased migration, as judged by increased colony diameter in the presence of EGF. However, the effect of EGF on cell locomotion was rarely accompanied by any effect on cell proliferation. It was concluded that EGF exerts a preferential effect on cell migration in human embryonal carcinoma cells in vitro.
abstract_ja: ヒト胎児性癌由来細胞株（Tera-2）のクローンに対する上皮増殖因子（EGF）の効果を検討しました。細胞はクローン密度で播種し、血清およびEGFの有無下で細胞運動と増殖を調べました。50 ng/mlのEGF添加により、コロニー径の増大で示される遊走の増加がみられました。一方、EGFの細胞運動への効果が細胞増殖に伴うことは稀でした。以上より、EGFはヒト胎児性癌細胞においてin vitroで増殖よりも遊走を優先的に促進すると結論しました。
